gaps.construct: an error stored in a struct field and compared against the sentinel io.EOF
gaps.description: Scribe failures exist only as names in `fails with` / `fail with` / `on failure`; they are not values. A closed `choice ScanError` stands in, which cannot hold arbitrary errors returned by the wrapped io.Reader (approximated by a `ReaderError with reason as Text` variant).
No interface or open sum type exists, so the set of storable errors is fixed when ScanError is declared.

gaps.construct: s.err == nil || s.err == io.EOF in one boolean test
gaps.description: A maybe value cannot be tested inline (`err of scanner is nothing` is not shown as valid) and its payload needs `choose`, so a one-line condition becomes a choose with two branches and a duplicated set line.
No methods; the receiver becomes an `editable` parameter. This works but loses method-call syntax and grouping with the type.

notes: Small function, but it shows that Scribe has no 'error value' concept: any API that records, defers or compares errors (bufio, database drivers, retry loops) must invent a parallel choice type outside the failure system. Consider either letting failures be first-class values of a choice, or allowing `is nothing` / `is some` tests on maybe values without a full choose.
